title: The Oriental Keyboard
subtitle: A Synthesizer/Sampler with full quartertone capability
paragraphs: The Oriental Keyboard is the successor of the org, and it came to the market toward the end of the 20th century. Its strength was that it could imitate sounds from various traditional Arabic instruments by sampling them, and as such the player could summon a Mijwiz, a Qanun, or even a Saxophone at the touch of a button.

Most synthesizer companies (like Roland, Yamaha, GEM, Kawai, Korg and Ketron) manufacture Oriental Keyboard models, and include a built-in electronic rhythm generator where the player can supplement their melody/chords with iqa‘at pre-recorded from sampled Arabic Percussion Instruments. This makes the Oriental Keyboard a very powerful and versatile instrument, and an essential one in Arabic pop and dance music.
The oriental keyboard is able to play a quartertone on any of the 12 notes of the keyboard simply by pressing a switch.

The Oriental Keyboard is the successor of the org , and it came to the market toward the end of the 20 th century. Its strength was that it could imitate sounds from various traditional Arabic instruments by sampling them, and as such the player could summon a Mijwiz , a Qanun , or even a Saxophone at the touch of a button. Most synthesizer companies (like Roland, Yamaha, GEM, Kawai, Korg and Ketron) manufacture Oriental Keyboard models, and include a built-in electronic rhythm generator where the player can supplement their melody/chords with iqa‘at pre-recorded from sampled Arabic Percussion Instruments. This makes the Oriental Keyboard a very powerful and versatile instrument, and an essential one in Arabic pop and dance music. 12 switches to lower each note on the keyboard by a quartertone The oriental keyboard is able to play a quartertone on any of the 12 notes of the keyboard simply by pressing a switch. Aw‘idak The National Arab Orchestra (U.S.A.) performing Su‘ad Muhammad's song Aw‘idak in an arrangement that includes the Oriental Keyboard and the Electric Guitar alongside traditional Arabic instruments. Shamstep by 47Soul Pan-Palestinian group 47Soul added an interesting twist to the normal usage of the Oriental Keyboard by using sound effects to create a new genre of techno- dabke , as in their hit song Shamstep .
